definitions.time_of_day: Night 00:00-05:59, Morning 06:00-11:59, Afternoon 12:00-17:59, Evening 18:00-23:59 (hour of Date).
definitions.season: Winter Dec-Feb, Spring Mar-May, Summer Jun-Aug, Fall Sep-Nov (by month of Date).
definitions.crime_category: Violent: ASSAULT, BATTERY, ROBBERY, HOMICIDE, CRIM SEXUAL ASSAULT, CRIMINAL SEXUAL ASSAULT, KIDNAPPING. Property: THEFT, BURGLARY, MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT, CRIMINAL DAMAGE, ARSON. Other: everything else.
definitions.arrest_rate: Arrest=TRUE rows / all rows in scope.

windows.method: Contiguous runs of >=60 days with >=200 records/day (windows.dense_windows), trimmed to whole calendar months. Outside these runs the file holds only 300-900 records/month.

source.provenance: Provided by the competition organisers. Column layout matches the City of Chicago Data Portal dataset 'Crimes - 2001 to Present' (Chicago Police Dept.); confirm before citing as such.

assumptions: Excel-converted Date cells were read day-first and are swapped back (month<->day).
Handout KPIs use the whole dataset (ground rules); deeper analysis uses the two dense windows.
CRIM SEXUAL ASSAULT and CRIMINAL SEXUAL ASSAULT are one offence under two labels; merged only in the harmonised column.
Timestamps at exactly 00:00/12:00 are treated as possible placeholders in sensitivity analyses, never dropped from handout metrics.
No population or area denominators exist in the data, so no per-capita statements are made.
p-values are secondary: with n ~ 10^5-10^6 effect sizes and CIs are reported; multiple comparisons use Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.
limitations: File is a truncated slice (Excel row limit); only two periods are dense.
Window B has ~0% coordinates; arrest outcomes in recent months may be incomplete.
